To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
podocarpic acids are not effective antitumor agents.
podocarpic acids and their derivatives possess significant in vitro antitumor activity, but are not active in vivo against L1210 leukemia in mice.
podocarpic derivatives have significant cytotoxicity against human epidermoid nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells, but no significant antitumor activities against L1210 or P388 lymphoid leukemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of podolactones and related podocaric acid derivatives and with the evaluation of their biological activities.
the synthesis of novel compounds related to the naturally occurring podocarpic acids and the evaluation of their biological activities, especially their antitumor properties.

the synthesis of a series of podolactone and podocarpic derivatives, the evaluation of these derivatives for cytotoxic activity against human epidermoid nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells in vitro and the assessment of the antitumoral activity in vivo against L1210 leukemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the podocarpic derivatives are not useful as anticancer drugs.
the podocarpic acids, in the forms examined, have not demonstrated significant antileukemic properties in the mouse.
podocarpic acids are of limited value in the treatment of human cancer.
